master:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: finished painted MASTER REFERENCE sprite for EVO: Living World, a premium hand-drawn 2D prehistoric underwater side-scroller.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Image 1 is the EXACT neutral-pose geometry reference exported from the actual fish rig. Repaint this same right-facing fish in place, keeping its overall proportions, fin locations, eye location, mouth hinge, tail location and horizontal baseline. Preserve its identity. Refine ugly angular joins into natural flowing anatomy without redesigning it as a different species.
Image 2 (the luminous clam) is a STYLE reference only: confident flowing dark ink contours, rich yet restrained painted color planes, subtle dry-brush shading, premium atmospheric 2D game art. Do not add any shell or pearl to the fish.

PRIMARY REQUEST:
Create a vastly more beautiful, cohesive painted version of the neutral fish. One single complete fish, side profile, facing RIGHT, mouth almost closed in the neutral pose. No labels or alternatives. It must look like a lovingly art-directed game creature with one continuous living body, not separately outlined shapes assembled together.

DESIGN:
An elegant, compact prehistoric fish with a subtly arched back, flowing tapered tail peduncle and a small forked fin. Keep reference fin placement and broad proportions. Sculpt the head and cheek into the body. A readable small luminous ivory-and-dark eye at the same reference position, naturally seated in the head instead of a pasted-on round button. The reference has a large C-shaped outlined gill flap; replace its visual treatment with a tapered gill fold and a soft integrated cheek plane, no thick closed ring or standalone plate around the head. Fin roots emerge from beneath the skin. The jaw is naturally attached beneath the snout; a restrained dark mouth slit with a few tiny teeth is enough. No silly smile, no rubber lips.

STYLE:
Original hand-inked and hand-painted 2D metroidvania art with Hollow Knight-like graphic clarity and flowing organic design, and the restrained painted surface quality of the clam reference. This is a GAME SPRITE. Deliberately designed large forms, variable-weight dark contours, quiet broad brushwork, selective crisp edges. Mostly three or four broad value groups. The fish must stay immediately legible at only 45 to 90 screen pixels wide. Put the visual richness into contour, volumes and overlap, not microdetail.

PALETTE / PAINT:
Near-neutral cool slate-gray skin suitable for later game tinting, dark charcoal upper back, medium silver-gray flanks, softly illuminated pale gray belly, slightly warm gray translucent fin membranes, restrained ivory eye accent. Broad softly painted light from above. Keep enough midtone brightness to read against dark teal water. No glossy plastic or photorealistic wet material.

EVOLUTION CONSTRAINTS:
Leave the flank as a clean smooth painted base. NO scales, scale arcs, camouflage stripes, armor plates, scars, spots, ridges or decorative repeated patterns anywhere on the body: these are dynamically layered by the game. The neck and snout must have broad quiet shapes that tolerate mesh stretching. Only a few fin rays. No baked environmental shadow or glow.

OUTPUT:
Transparent RGBA PNG. Preserve the reference canvas/aspect, ideally 1712 by 960, preserving relative placement and clear transparent margin. One complete neutral fish, all fins and tail visible, no cropped edges, no water, background, rocks, ground, shadow beneath the fish, border, text, measurements, wireframe or presentation sheet.
Avoid: vector clipart, procedural polygon bands, thick uniform marker outlines around every part, South Park cutout look, realistic fish photography, 3D renders, detailed scales, busy concept art.

parts.body:
Production texture for the existing fish rig of EVO: Living World. Input 1 is the EXACT PART TEMPLATE to repaint in place: preserve its original canvas proportions, placement, silhouette, negative spaces and transparent padding. Input 2 is the finished assembled fish, STYLE AND MATERIAL REFERENCE ONLY. Match its flowing dark ink edge, softly hand-painted cool slate-gray skin, restrained silver-gray light and simple broad value shapes. The artwork must be readable when the complete fish is displayed only 45 to 90 screen pixels wide. Produce only the isolated part from input 1, never the complete fish from input 2. True transparent RGBA background; clean alpha edges; no background, text, labels, wireframe, border, floor, detached glows or shadow. No scales, camouflage, armor plates, spots, repeated body patterns or scars. No photorealism, 3D, vector clipart or shiny plastic.
PART: body + upper head + tail peduncle + caudal tail fin, all one continuous texture. This is deliberately an EYeless, JAWless, otherwise FINless body surface: no eye or eye socket, no lower jaw, no mouth cavity, no dorsal/pectoral/anal/pelvic fins, no gill lines or gill plate; these are separate textures. Keep ONLY the caudal tail fin already present at the LEFT. The lower-right notch under the upper snout is a real transparent cutout where the separate jaw fits; keep that exact negative space and the upper lip height. REMOVE the old scale arcs, vertical pattern bands, decorative lines and all tiny teeth from the template. Paint a clean continuous base skin, darker back, gently lit slate-gray flank and a subtle pale belly; a few caudal fin rays in warm neutral gray. No nostril or neck details that stretch. Preserve the original broad body contour, tail-root connection and the reference margin; do not center or crop around the opaque shape. Original canvas 1575 x 648. Preserve the 2.4306:1 canvas aspect.
